NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

DRAFT MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 12, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR HUFF called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by PV Hills Nursery School.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Donald Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Gabrielle Swain

4.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-J AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF NOVEMBER & DECEMBER 2023

  APPROVED WARRANTS 66825 THROUGH 66929 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $1,381,003.35 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 110423 THROUGH
  110523; 120123 THROUGH 120323; IN THE AMOUNT OF $222,030.62 FOR
  A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $1,603,033.97 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF OCTOBER 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  APPROVED THE BUDGET AMENDMENTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024.

 F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 14, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

J.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS BOARD MEETING
  HIGHLIGHTS OF NOVEMBER 16, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

5.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PRESENTATION TO OUTGOING MAYOR BRITT HUFF

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ thanked and recognized MAYOR HUFF by briefly highlighting
her many accomplishments as Mayor over the last year.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ presented MAYOR HUFF with gifts including a
commemorative framed photo of the 19th Amendment Dedication, and a gavel plaque
including her most recent year as Mayor.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ introduced those present to make presentations to MAYOR
HUFF:

  - Karen Calderon from the office of Congressman Ted Lieu
  - Los Angeles County Board Supervisor Janice Hahn
  - City of Rolling Hills Council Member Bea Dieringer
  - Jeff Kiernan, Regional Public Affairs Manager, Los Angeles County Division for the
  League of California Cities
  - Palos Verdes Peninsula School District Board Member Linda Kurt
  - Palos Verdes Library District Trustee Bob Parke
  - Los Angeles County Fire Department Battalion Chief Mike Lewis

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ indicated that certificates of recognition for MAYOR HUFF
were also received from the offices of Senator Ben Allen and Assemblymember Al
Muratsuchi, the City of Rancho Palos Verdes, and the City of Palos Verdes Estates.

MAYOR HUFF thanked all of the dignitaries, her fellow Council Members and City staff, and
commented on her year as Mayor.

6.  CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

MAYOR HUFF nominated MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ to serve as the City’s next Mayor.

  VELVETH SCHMITZ APPOINTED MAYOR BY ACCLAMATION.

MAYOR SCHMITZ nominated COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA to serve as the City’s next
MAYOR PRO TEM.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 12, 2023
   DEBBY STEGURA APPOINTED MAYOR PRO TEM BY ACCLAMATION.

  ***

At 7:49 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting to a brief reception.

MAYOR SCHMITZ called the meeting back to order at 8:05 p.m.

  ***

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Martin Gombert, Administrator for the Palos Verdes Transit Authority (PVTA), spoke regarding
the free New Year’s Eve bus services offered across the Peninsula.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  REQUEST TO APPROVE A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA) FOR
  USER FEE UPDATE - COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AND PUBLIC WORKS
  DEPARTMENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council award a Professional Services Agreement
  (PSA) to Matrix Consulting Group to conduct a comprehensive User Fee Study for
  the Community Development and Public Works Departments, to the satisfaction of
  the City Attorney.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  AWARD A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA) TO MATRIX
  CONSULTING GROUP TO CONDUCT A COMPREHENSIVE USER FEE
  STUDY FOR THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AND PUBLIC WORKS
  DEPARTMENTS, TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  2023 PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (PMS) REPORT UPDATE PREPARED
  BY WILLDAN ENGINEERING

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the 2023 Pavement
  Management System (PMS) Report prepared by Willdan Engineering.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),and
introduced Ron Stein from Willdan Engineering who provided a summary of the PMS report.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA inquired about permeable pavement as a future option.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  RECEIVED AND FILED THE 2023 PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
  (PMS) REPORT PREPARED BY WILLDAN ENGINEERING.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
DECEMBER 12, 2023
 So ordered by MAYOR SCHMITZ.

C.  REQUEST TO APPROVE A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA) FOR
  TRANSTECH ENGINEERS, INC. TO PROVIDE BIDDING SUPPORT AND PROJECT
  MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER
  REPLACEMENT PROJECT. LOCATION: SOUTHWEST CORNER OF PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE NORTH & PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST (27305 PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE EAST)

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Award a Professional Services Agreement
  (PSA) to Transtech Engineers, Inc., for Project Bidding and Construction
  Management Services, for the George F Canyon Nature Center Project (all to the
  satisfaction of the City Attorney) in the amount of $249,700.00; and 2) Direct staff to
  solicit construction bids for the George F Canyon Nature Center Project.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the comparison of hours estimated between HR
Green and Transtech Engineers, with almost 300 more hours estimated by HR Green. Public
Works Director Wahba noted that staff works closely with the coordination of hours and billing
for the project, and that staff feels comfortable with Transtech’s estimated hours.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER echoed COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF’s concerns. City
Attorney Davis explained the not-to-exceed amount included within the Professional Services
Agreement.

Public Works Director Wahba noted that the $250,000 is included in the total cost of $3.99M,
in response to MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA.

MAYOR SCHMITZ clarified that the complexities of the management of this project
necessitates an outside firm, and highlighted the amount of work staff has done towards finding
grants and donations for this project.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  1) AWARD A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA) TO
  TRANSTECH ENGINEERS, INC., FOR PROJECT BIDDING AND
  CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES, FOR THE GEORGE F
  CANYON NATURE CENTER PROJECT (ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF
  THE CITY ATTORNEY) IN THE AMOUNT OF $249,700.00; AND 2) DIRECT
  STAFF TO SOLICIT CONSTRUCTION BIDS FOR THE GEORGE F CANYON
  NATURE CENTER PROJECT.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

D.  RESOLUTION NO. 2561 - AUTHORIZING PARTICIPATION IN THE CALRECYCLE
  SB 1383 LOCAL ASSISTANCE GRANT PROGRAM

  Recommendation: That City Council adopt the attached Resolution No. 2561,
  authorizing staff to apply to CalRecycle’s SB 1383 Local Assistance Grant program
  and designating the City Manager, or his designee, as a “Signature Authority.”

Administrative Aide Swain provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
DECEMBER 12, 2023
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2561, AUTHORIZING STAFF TO APPLY TO
  CALRECYCLE’S SB 1383 LOCAL ASSISTANCE GRANT PROGRAM AND
  DESIGNATING THE CITY MANAGER, OR HIS DESIGNEE, AS A
  “SIGNATURE AUTHORITY.”

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2561 by title.

E.  ADOPTION OF FY 2023-24 PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE

  Recommendation: That City Council approve a Publicly Available Pay Schedule for
  the 2023-24 fiscal year in accordance with California Public Employees' Retirement
  System (CalPERS) regulations.

Administrative Aide Swain provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE A PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE FOR THE 2023-24
  FISCAL YEAR IN ACCORDANCE WITH CALIFORNIA PUBLIC EMPLOYEES'
  RETIREMENT SYSTEM (CALPERS) REGULATIONS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

10.  OLD BUSINESS

  EMERGENCY ARISING FROM SIGNIFICANT LAND MOVEMENT ALONG AND IN
  THE VICINITY OF PEARTREE LANE IN THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2562 continuing the

  APPROVE A PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE FOR THE 2023-24

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the California Association of Councils of Governments
(CALCOG) State meeting in Riverside on Friday and was elected 1st Vice President.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that the entire Council will be attending the California
Contract Cities Association’s Legislative Tour in January in Sacramento.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA attended the Clean Power Alliance (CPA) Board meeting and
attended the SBCCOG Steering/Board Committee meeting in December. She also participated
